newsitem.title: LATVIA: VENTSPILS NOT SEEKING BIG STRATEGIC INVESTOR.
newsitem.headline: VENTSPILS NOT SEEKING BIG STRATEGIC INVESTOR.

text.p: Latvia, currently in the process of selling major oil terminal Ventspils Nafta, is not looking for a strategic investor, either Western or Eastern, the privatisation agency (LPA) said on Wednesday.
"There is no quota of Ventspils Nafta shares set aside for a strategic investor," Janis Naglis, LPA director general, told a news conference.
"Ventpils Nafta does not need a strategic investor to secure its development," he added.
There has been much speculation that the large Russian oil companies such as Yukos and Lukoil want a stake in Ventspils as it is one of the main outlets for their output.
"The company has been managed convincingly and with precision, showing the highest return on capital among the state companies," he said.
Ventspils Nafta, the biggest outlet for Russian crude and oil products in the region, had its privatisation rules approved by the agency on April 29.
All investors can take part in share auctions, either in the public offer for vouchers or the seven percent stake to be placed abroad, Naglis said.
He said that the future of Ventspils did not depend on one of the big Russian companies being a shareholder.

"Ventspils' workload will depend solely on the quality of its services, how well we prevent theft from the pipe-line, on the performance of Ventspils port and how soon large tankers can eneter it," Naglis said.
Ventspils is deepening its port to 17.5 metres from 12.5 metres, which will allow tankers of 120,000 tonnes be loaded there compared with 80,000 tonnes now.
